answer: The wharf only takes ballots carrying one signal: a receipt for real paid work finished in the last 30 days — a completed $5 Fiverr order, a paid Upwork milestone, a bounty-paid pull request — checked live via the platform's public API, from a payer no other ballot used. A farm floating 10,000 fake ballots sinks at that dock: it needs 10,000 distinct receipts, $50,000 at the $5 floor both marketplaces publish, plus real hours per job, and a receipt shown twice gets both ballots rejected. Like a sable pelt, no two receipts share a pattern — a farm without $50,000 of real work stays ashore.
